claims.text: The initial Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy is a single-phase fcc high-entropy alloy.
The initial alloy has low coercivity because of suppressed orbital moments.
Controlled annealing can precipitate a Ti-rich L2_1 ordered phase while retaining the fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix.
Fe2TiNi or a similar Heusler-type compound is a plausible Ti-rich L2_1 precipitate in this alloy.
A 10-20 vol% L2_1 fraction will preserve a precipitate-containing fcc matrix rather than produce effectively single-phase L2_1 behavior.
The fcc matrix and L2_1 phase will remain structurally and magnetically stable from 300 K to 600 K.
The L2_1 precipitates will be coherent or semi-coherent with the fcc matrix.
L2_1 precipitates will create local strain fields that modify magnetic anisotropy.
The fcc/L2_1 interfaces will introduce strong exchange coupling and magnetic anisotropy.
The L2_1 precipitates will pin domain walls and thereby increase coercivity.
The secondary phase will stabilize a non-collinear magnetic ground state.
Ti enrichment in the L2_1 phase will locally restore or enhance the orbital-moment contribution.
An fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy containing 10-20 vol% L2_1 precipitates will have coercivity greater than 100 Oe.
The dual-phase alloy will retain high yield strength through precipitation hardening.
The magnetic ordering temperature of the dual-phase alloy will remain well above room temperature.
The single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti baseline has coercivity below 50 Oe.
L2_1 fractions above approximately 44 vol% approach single-phase behavior and constitute a failure boundary.
Current thermodynamic databases have insufficient accuracy for predicting L2_1 stability.
Comparing nominally 0%, 10%, 20%, 45%, and 85% L2_1 specimens provides a control series for distinguishing single-phase from dual-phase magnetic contributions.
Failure to exceed 100 Oe at confirmed 10-20 vol% L2_1 is a decisive falsification outcome.

contradictions.description: The operating regime is described as significantly above room temperature, but the stated example range begins at 300 K, which is approximately room temperature.
